vulnerabilities.description: Auth token obtained but not used in API request. getAccessTokenSilently() is called but the token is never added to request headers. This bypasses authentication for the /api/chat endpoint, allowing unauthenticated access.
vulnerabilities.code: const token = await getAccessTokenSilently(); ... fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/chat`, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(...) })
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized access to chat API, potential data exposure

vulnerabilities.description: Auth token obtained but not passed to API request. getAccessTokenSilently() is called in a try-catch but the token variable is never used in the fetch headers.
vulnerabilities.impact: County validation endpoint may lack proper authentication, allowing bypass

vulnerabilities.description: Client-side payment bypass via NODE_ENV check. Sends `skipPayment: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` to backend, which could bypass payment validation if development mode is misconfigured or NODE_ENV is compromised.
vulnerabilities.impact: Payment validation could be bypassed; users could access paid features without payment

vulnerabilities.description: Client-side MIME type validation only. Validates file type using `!ALLOWED_TYPES[file.type]` which is trivially spoofable. MIME types can be forged by renaming files. While the CLAUDE.md mentions server-side 'magic-byte sniff', client validation is weak.
vulnerabilities.impact: Malicious files could potentially bypass validation; relies entirely on server-side validation

vulnerabilities.description: TOS acceptance status stored in localStorage with user ID as key: `tos_accepted_${user?.sub}`. LocalStorage is accessible to any JavaScript and XSS attacks could forge acceptance. Should use httpOnly cookies or server-side sessions.
vulnerabilities.impact: XSS vulnerability could allow attackers to mark users as TOS-accepted, bypassing legal requirements

vulnerabilities.description: Error details sent to window.logError without sanitization. Stack traces, component names, and user URLs are exposed. Could leak sensitive system information or PII.
vulnerabilities.code: window.logError({ error: error.toString(), errorInfo: errorInfo.componentStack, timestamp, userAgent, url })
vulnerabilities.impact: Error logs could expose sensitive information, stack traces, application structure

vulnerabilities.description: Uses ReactMarkdown to render TOS content. If markdown content were ever user-controlled or sourced from untrusted input, could be XSS vector. Verify TERMS_OF_SERVICE content is always trusted.
vulnerabilities.impact: XSS if markdown content becomes user-controlled; could steal cookies/tokens

vulnerabilities.description: Payment amount is set on client side. While Stripe validates server-side (per CLAUDE.md: 'server-side pricing only'), the client passes documentType which determines pricing. Should verify amount validation happens server-side.
vulnerabilities.code: const [amount, setAmount] = useState(7900); ... body: JSON.stringify({ documentType, documentId })
vulnerabilities.impact: If server-side validation is weak, users could potentially specify lower prices

vulnerabilities.description: API endpoint `/api/templates/states` is called without authentication. Endpoint appears to be public but should verify it's intentionally public and doesn't expose sensitive data.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure if endpoint contains sensitive jurisdiction data; generally low if intentional public endpoint

vulnerabilities.description: loginWithRedirect called with appState but verify PKCE flow is properly configured in Auth0. Missing state/nonce could be CSRF vulnerability.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential CSRF if Auth0 PKCE not properly configured; low risk with @auth0/nextjs-auth0

recommendations.title: Fix Missing Authentication Headers
recommendations.description: Add Authorization header with Auth0 token to all API requests. Update ChatInterface.js and CountyValidationInput.js to include: `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` }`

recommendations.title: Remove Client-Side Payment Bypass
recommendations.description: Remove the `skipPayment` parameter from GenerateButton.js. Payment validation must ONLY occur server-side. Never allow clients to skip payment checks.

recommendations.title: Implement Server-Side File Type Validation
recommendations.description: Ensure /api/evidence/upload endpoint performs magic-byte validation (not just MIME check). Use libraries like file-type to verify actual file content. Client should only accept uploaded files from server response.

recommendations.title: Move TOS Acceptance to Secure Storage
recommendations.description: Replace localStorage-based TOS tracking with server-side session storage or httpOnly cookies. Implement API endpoint /api/auth/tos-accept that creates tamper-proof server-side record.

recommendations.title: Sanitize Error Reporting
recommendations.description: In ErrorBoundary.js, sanitize error details before sending. Don't include component stack, URLs with sensitive params, or userAgent details. Send only error type/code and generic message.

recommendations.title: Verify ReactMarkdown Security
recommendations.description: Confirm TERMS_OF_SERVICE content in lib/content/termsOfService.js is always hardcoded/trusted. If ever loading from database, implement markdown sanitization using `sanitize-html` with strict whitelist.

recommendations.title: Verify Server-Side Payment Validation
recommendations.description: Audit /api/payment/create-intent endpoint to ensure it validates pricing server-side from PRICING_CONFIG (per lib/api/stripe.ts), never trusting client-supplied amounts.

recommendations.title: Document Public API Endpoints
recommendations.description: Add comments to public endpoints (/api/templates/*, /api/counties/*) to clarify they're intentionally unauthenticated. Verify they don't expose sensitive data.

recommendations.title: Enable Content Security Policy
recommendations.description: Verify next.config.mjs properly sets CSP headers. Should include: `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (for wasm), restrict frame-ancestors, disable inline scripts.

recommendations.title: Add CSRF Token Validation
recommendations.description: For POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints, implement CSRF token validation. Next.js middleware can verify origin header, but explicit token-based CSRF protection recommended.

strengths: Parameterized queries used throughout (SQL injection protected)
Row-Level Security (RLS) enabled at database level
Stripe payment integration follows best practices (Stripe Elements, server-side validation)
Next.js App Router provides built-in CSRF protection
Environment variables properly separated from code
File upload has size limits and MIME type checking (client-side)
